Ana (support): @Max heads-up — ACME (Priya) just escalated a p99 latency spike that correlates with GPU OOMs on their dedicated pool. They see lots of retries and increased client errors. logs pasted below. :grimacing:

Priya (ACME): Happening under steady concurrency ~120, many long chats (1.5k-2.5k tokens). We see repeated alloc failures and a bunch of retries from our side. Impacting production users.

DevBot: deploy-pool-acme-1 finished at 1769795600 (no config changes flagged)

Max (runtime): Can you paste the runtime memory / kv stats? my hunch: KV cache growth + slab fragmentation -> OOM -> allocator slow paths -> p99 spikes.

Ana (support): Logs: ```
[1769799998] gpu_mem_used=41.2GB gpu_mem_total=48.0GB
[1769799998] kv_cache_entries=12,340,121 kv_cache_bytes=29.4GB
[1769799998] slab_free_frag=6.8GB slab_alloc_fail=312
[1769799998] allocator_compactions=0 compaction_fail=27
[1769799998] p95_ms=620 p99_ms=1420 retries=187
```

Jia (sre): +1 to Max. allocator_compactions=0 is suspicious. Any recent model or tokenizer change that increases prefix reuse?

Priya (ACME): No model bump. Workload got heavier this week (more long conversations). We do reuse prefixes a lot (context windows with system prompts).

Max (runtime): Repro steps I used locally: run rload with 150 concurrency, each session ~2k tokens, enable prefix reuse. Observed KV growth to 30GB then slab fragmentation -> first allocs hit slow path and p99 shoots up. Quick reproduction command: 
```
rload --target pool-acme-1 --concurrency 150 --seq-len 2000 --prefix-reuse=high --duration 15m
```

Max (runtime): Short-term mitigations we can apply without code: enable live KV eviction + lower kv_max_bytes for the pool, toggle prefetch=false. Also enable slab compaction schedule and/or run a one-off defrag on one node. Longer-term: implement per-tenant KV caps and background slab defrag.

Ana (support): Customer asks for non-disruptive option first — they prefer no node restarts. Can we do the live config changes?

Max (runtime): Yes. Control plane exposes a live pool policy update. I'll push an "aggressive-evict" policy that turns on LRU eviction and reduces kv_max_bytes to 16GB. No restart required. Also can set slab_compact_frequency=60s (live param). I'll schedule the change now if we agree.

Jia (sre): I'll prepare a safe compaction playbook in case compaction exacerbates tail latencies. Plan: drain one GPU at a time, start defrag during off-peak, set max-duration=300s. Command snippet: 
```
# run from runtime pod
/opt/runtime/bin/slabctl defrag --max-duration=300 --max-steps=5
```

Ana (support): Action items: (1) @Max roll live policy to aggressive-evict on pool-acme-1 within 10m (2) @Jia schedule one-node compaction & provide ETA (3) @Ana update Priya with mitigation steps and ETA. Priya — can you confirm we can apply eviction live?

Priya (ACME): Confirmed — okay to apply the eviction policy. We'll accept short transient retries.

Max (runtime): rolled aggressive-evict -> pool-acme-1 at 1769800300. Changes: kv_max_bytes=16GB, kv_evict_mode=LRU, prefetch=false, slab_compact_frequency=60s. Monitoring now.

DevBot: alert resolved: gpu_mem_pressure_pool-acme-1 at 1769800355

Jia (sre): Started compaction on runtime-7 at 1769800400. Running defrag with max-duration=300s. Observed immediate drop in fragmentation metric. p99 down to ~380ms currently.

Max (runtime): After eviction + compaction we see KV bytes drop ~12GB and alloc_fail_count cleared. p95/p99 trending back to normal. Will keep an eye for regressions.

Ana (support): Thanks team. I'll send ACME a summary and add follow-up work: per-tenant kv caps, automatic slab defrag scheduling, and runtime knob docs.

Priya (ACME): Thanks, team. We'll monitor and report if anything else pops up.

Jia (sre): Filing follow-up: create RFC for automated defrag + tenant-level kv quota. Assigning to @Max.

Max (runtime): ack. Will draft RFC and propose telemetry alerts for slab_free_frag > 5GB and kv_bytes growth rate > 1GB/min.

Ana (support): Closing loop here for now. Will reopen if customer sees more issues. :thumbsup:
